None of the three solutions gives the correct formula. This rests partly on recalled values rather than a derivation.

- **Small case e = 3:** The cyclic group Z₈ has 6 skew morphisms (4 automorphisms and 2 proper ones). Solution 1 gives 2³ + 2 = 10 and Solution 2 gives 2·4 = 8, so both fail at e = 3. Solution 3 gives 2³ − 2 = 6, so it matches here.
- **Why Solution 3 still fails:** Its classification of the skew morphisms of Z₂ₑ is incomplete. It lists only one family of proper skew morphisms, of the form "fix even x, add t to odd x". Computed lists of skew morphisms of cyclic groups show many more for larger 2-powers. I recall Z₁₆ having 22, though I could not verify this, whereas Solution 3 predicts 14. The true count grows roughly quadratically in 2ᵉ, not linearly as 2ᵉ − 2 does.

CHOICE: NONE
